newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ABB CEO SAYS PERFORMANCE STRONG.
newsitem.headline: ABB CEO SAYS PERFORMANCE STRONG.

text.p: Goran Lindahl, chief executive officer of ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG, described the company's performance in the first half of 1997 as "strong" and said the order intake was encouraging for the future.
Lindahl said ABB's result in the first half of 1997 was "in line with what he had promised" and he pointed to the strong growth rate in new orders.
New orders rose 14 percent in the first half to $20.0 billion. In local currency terms orders rose 21 percent.
"This is a very good growth rate and show the effort to penetrate markets, especially the emerging markets, is giving good rewards," Lindahl told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Lindahl noted that all ABB's business segments, including Power Generation, had showed improved operating earnings in the first half, another positive sign.
"This is a strong performance in an in-between year. This is the second year of a downturn," Lindahl said, referring to the impact on ABB of Western Europe's recent recession.
Regarding the net profit increase of two percent, Lindahl said currencies were difficult to forecast, but it was more important to look at the performance in local currencies.
"Look at the operating performance and look at the currencies; this is a strong performance," Lindahl said.

ABB's first half group net profit rose two percent to $567 million, but expressed in local currencies it rose 12 percent. The strong dollar has the effect of reducing ABB's group results, which are reported in U.S. dollars.
First half operating earnings rose three percent to $1.09 billion, but the increase was 11 percent in local currencies.
